business_name: Youngstown HVAC Services: Heating & Air Conditioning
audit_headline: The profile lists 'General Contractor' as the primary category instead of an HVAC-specific category, which weakens relevance for heating and air conditioning searches in Youngstown.
summary: Youngstown HVAC Services has a strong 4.9-star rating from 9 reviews, with recent feedback highlighting responsiveness and professionalism. However, the profile's primary category is set to 'General Contractor' rather than an HVAC-specific category, and there is no website linked — both of which limit discoverability when potential customers search for heating and air conditioning services. The profile also has zero photos visible, and the lack of a web presence means no additional trust signals or contact paths beyond the phone number.

sections.title: Google Business Profile
sections.summary: The profile has hours listed and a phone number, but critical elements for HVAC discoverability are missing or misconfigured.

findings.observation: The primary category is set to 'General Contractor' rather than an HVAC-specific category like 'HVAC contractor' or 'Heating contractor.' This is a major relevance mismatch: the business name explicitly includes 'HVAC Services: Heating & Air Conditioning,' but Google sees it primarily as a general contractor.
findings.recommendation: Change the primary category to 'HVAC contractor' (or the closest HVAC-specific option Google offers). This is a recognized trust and relevance signal for heating and air conditioning searches.

findings.observation: The profile shows zero photos. Visual content is a known local-search trust signal, and competitors with job photos, team images, or truck shots will have a stronger profile presence.
findings.recommendation: Upload at least 10-15 photos: completed jobs, your team, your service vehicles with branding, and before-and-after shots of HVAC installations or repairs. This helps potential customers recognize your business and builds credibility.

findings.observation: No website is linked on the profile. This means no additional information, no click-to-call from a mobile site, no service details, and no structured data to reinforce your location and trade.
findings.recommendation: Either link an existing website or create a simple one-page site with your services, service area (Youngstown and surrounding areas), phone number as a clickable link, and your hours. Even a basic site is a relevance and trust signal.

findings.observation: Hours are listed and cover evenings and weekends (7 AM–8 PM weekdays, 9:30 AM–7 PM weekends), which is strong for HVAC emergencies.

The profile is marked as a physical location (not service-area-only) at 3325 Mahoning Ave, Youngstown, OH. If this is an office or shop customers can visit, that's fine; if it's a home address or you serve customers at their locations, consider switching to service-area-business mode to avoid confusion.
findings.recommendation: Verify that the address is appropriate for customer visits. If it's not a public-facing location, edit the profile to hide the address and list your service areas instead.

sections.title: Reviews & Reputation
sections.summary: The 4.9-star rating from 9 reviews is excellent, and recent reviews emphasize speed and professionalism, but review volume is low and momentum has stalled.

findings.observation: The profile has 9 total reviews with a 4.9-star rating. The most recent reviews are from 11 months ago, meaning no new reviews have appeared in nearly a year. For an HVAC business, this suggests either low job volume or that customers aren't being asked to leave reviews.
findings.recommendation: After every completed job, ask satisfied customers to leave a Google review. Send a follow-up text or email with a direct link to your profile's review page. Fresh reviews signal active business and build trust with new searchers.

findings.observation: The three most recent reviews (all from 11 months ago) mention 'urgent heating problem' resolved quickly, 'professional, knowledgeable, and genuinely helpful,' and 'accommodating to our schedule.' These are strong service themes, but there's no way to verify from the API whether you've responded to any reviews.
findings.recommendation: Log into your Google Business Profile and check whether you've replied to all reviews. If not, respond to each one — thank the reviewer and reinforce a key service point (e.g. '24/7 emergency service'). Owner responses are a recognized engagement signal.

sections.title: Website & Online Presence
sections.summary: No website is linked, which eliminates a major trust and relevance channel for local search.

findings.observation: The profile has no website linked. This means potential customers have no way to learn about your services, see pricing or service-area details, or contact you outside of calling. It also means Google has no additional content to crawl that reinforces 'HVAC,' 'heating,' 'air conditioning,' and 'Youngstown.'
findings.recommendation: Create or link a website. At minimum, include: (1) a homepage <title> tag with 'HVAC' or 'Heating & Air Conditioning' and 'Youngstown, OH'; (2) your phone number as a clickable tel: link; (3) your service list; (4) LocalBusiness structured data with your name, address, phone, and hours. Even a single-page site is a known relevance signal.

findings.observation: With no website, there is no mobile-friendly contact path, no HTTPS trust indicator, and no way to capture leads outside of phone calls during business hours.
findings.recommendation: If you build a site, ensure it has a mobile viewport meta tag and click-to-call buttons. Many HVAC searches happen on mobile, often during an emergency.

sections.title: Call Handling & Contact Paths
sections.summary: A phone number is listed and hours cover evenings and weekends, but there is no way to verify how calls are handled after hours or when you're on a job.

findings.observation: The profile lists (330) 227-1434, and hours extend to 8 PM on weekdays and 7 PM on weekends. However, HVAC emergencies often happen outside these windows, and there is no indication of after-hours coverage or a missed-call text-back system.
findings.recommendation: Call your own number after 8 PM and on a Sunday evening to confirm what a customer hears. If calls go to voicemail with no callback promise, consider adding a message that offers a text-back option or an emergency line. Many HVAC leads are lost when a customer calls and hears silence or a generic voicemail.
